newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom lifted by Cellnet investment.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom lifted by Cellnet investment.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) shares rose on Thursday, following yesterday's reports that its unit Cellnet would invest one billion stg in its digital network over five years.
BT shares were up 11p at 397-1/2p at 1005 GMT in active morning trading in a rising market.
BT owns 60 percent of UK mobile telephone company Cellnet, whose spending plans were reported in Wednesday's Financial Times newspaper.
Analysts said the market had over-reacted somewhat, as the plans were in line with Cellnet's previous investments.
"It doesn't represent an increase in capital expenditure," said Oliver Ehrenberg of Robert Fleming Securities.

Salomon Brothers analyst Andrew Harrington called the investment "interesting but not significant". Harrington pointed out that shares in Securicor Group, which has a 40 percent stake in Cellnet were up only 1-1/2p at 270p by 1113 GMT.
The analyst put BT's rise down to possible short covering by arbitrageurs selling MCI stock and buying BT.
BT and MCI this week filed their merger plans for U.S. approval, fuelling anxiety over whether the deal would be allowed.
Other traders said the rise was also helped by BT Director Sir Peter Bonfield buying some 130,000 shares late on Wednesday under a renumeration plan.
By 1120 GMT, BT was up 15p at 401-1/2p.
